seoTitle: Free ISO Week Number Calculator for Any Date
metaDescription: Find the ISO 8601 week number and week-year of any date, where weeks start on Monday and week 1 holds the first Thursday. Free, in your browser.
intro: Pick a date. The tool shows its ISO 8601 week number, the week-based year and the weekday.
why: Planning calendars, payroll schedules, shipping notices and sprint boards often refer to week 37 rather than a date. The trouble is that week numbering is not universal: in some countries weeks start on Sunday and week 1 is the one containing 1 January. The ISO 8601 system, common across Europe and in business software, starts on Monday and makes week 1 the week with the first Thursday. As a result, the last days of December can belong to week 1 of the next year, and early January can sit in week 52 or 53 of the previous one. This calculator applies the ISO rule and shows the week-year, so edge cases are not a surprise. The date stays in your browser.
howTo: Read the ISO week number and the week-based year.
Check the weekday shown beside the date if you need to place it in the week.

faq.q: What is the ISO 8601 week rule?
faq.a: Weeks run Monday to Sunday, and week 1 is the week that contains the year's first Thursday, which is the same as the week containing 4 January.

faq.q: Why can 30 December be in week 1?
faq.a: Because the week belongs to the year that holds its Thursday. If Thursday falls on 2 January, the Monday before it, in late December, is part of week 1 of the new year.

faq.q: Is this the same as the week number in Excel or the US?
faq.a: Not always. US calendars and some Excel settings start weeks on Sunday and count the week with 1 January as week 1, so numbers can differ by one.
Yes. Some years have 53 ISO weeks, typically when 1 January falls on a Thursday, or on a Wednesday in a leap year.
